item.title: Stock Market News Today: Surprising Records Amid War
item.description:
Wall Street just did something almost nobody expected: it shrugged off a war. The stock market news today is dominated by a counterintuitive story — the S&P 500 and Nasdaq keep minting fresh record highs even as the Iran conflict continues, with the Dow joining the rally on hopes of a resolution.

Key Takeaways

  • The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at fresh records on Thursday, April 16, 2026, with the Dow rising on war-resolution hopes.
  • The Nasdaq extended its winning streak to 12 straight sessions — its longest run in nearly two decades.
  • Netflix tumbled after hours, while Abbott fell about 5% and Schwab dropped 10% despite record revenue.
  • A 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire lifted global futures heading into Friday.
  • Investors are rotating back into tech and semiconductors as AI-disruption fears fade.

Why the Stock Market Is Hitting Records Despite the Iran War

The headline looks strange at first glance: stock market news today shows equities at all-time highs while a shooting war is still underway. Yet that is exactly what CNBC, Yahoo Finance, and Kiplinger reported on Thursday.

item.title: Meta Stock Faces Turbulence: Landmark Lawsuit, Layoffs, and an AI Gamble
item.description:
What happens when the world’s largest social media company loses a landmark addiction lawsuit, announces hundreds of layoffs, and doubles down on a multi-billion-dollar AI bet — all in the same week?

Welcome to Meta Platforms in March 2026.

Key Takeaways

  • A Los Angeles jury ruled 10-to-2 that Meta and Google knew their platform designs were “dangerous” but failed to warn users, resulting in a $6 million verdict against the companies.
  • Meta is laying off hundreds of employees across key divisions as it redirects resources toward artificial intelligence.
  • Despite the turbulence, 42 analysts maintain a “Strong Buy” rating on META with a 12-month price target of $838.50 — roughly 49% above its current price.
  • Meta’s 2025 revenue hit $200.97 billion, up 22.17% year-over-year, though earnings dipped slightly by 3.05%.

Meta Stock Under Pressure: The Addiction Verdict

The biggest headline rocking META shares this week is a landmark U.S. lawsuit over social media addiction. A Los Angeles jury voted 10-to-2 that Meta and Google knew their platform designs were “dangerous” but failed to warn the plaintiffs.
